patients.label: 76-year-old woman with moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease and Graves’ disease treated with steroids and orbital radiotherapy
attribution_limitations: Three print artefacts appear in the source: "moderate-tosevere" in the abstract, "hyroid-stimulating hormone" and the drug name "omazeprole". They are kept as printed in evidence; the severity and indication labels are spaced prose.

The follow-up "in May" carries no year, and the visual acuity and colour vision improvement is dated only "a month after OR". The source does not say these are the same visit, and the May follow-up is not stated to be May 2015.
Selenium 200 mcg is only recommended, and the source does not say it was taken.

The methylprednisolone schedule "500 mg three times for the first week" does not state whether three doses were given in total or daily; the 250 mg per week step and the oral prednisolone taper have no stated start dates.

The source does not say whether the atrial fibrillation or the hyperthyroidism was later diagnosed as Graves’ disease, nor when the Graves’ diagnosis was made relative to the carbimazole and thyroxine prescriptions.

The improvement in left optic nerve function and reduced oedema follows the steroid sentence, and the later statements credit steroids with orbital radiotherapy for the visual improvement; the source gives no time for the first and does not separate the effect of each treatment.
The CT time is not stated; it follows the March 2015 sentence and precedes the steroid sentence, but the source gives no date or order word for it.
The authors state the patient may require further intervention after an extended period of disease inactivity; this is speculation, not a planned action, and is not recorded as a plan.
Free T4 12.6 is printed without a unit.
Increased eyelid inflammation and erythema occurred after the first three radiotherapy treatments, but the source does not state that radiotherapy caused it.
